scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which exceeds the standard 30-day refund policy.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Todd Anderson and I'm 75. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello, Mr. Anderson. I appreciate you reaching out, and I'm sorry to hear about the confusion regarding the charge while you were traveling. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide the email address associated with your account and the transaction ID or the date the charge occurred?
My email is tanderson@email.com and the charge was for $49.99 on October 15th.
Thank you, Todd. I have located your account. For security purposes, could you please confirm the last four digits of the payment method on file that was charged?

Thank you for verifying those details. I see here that your service cancellation was processed on day 34. Per our 'Terms of Service Section 4.2: Refund Eligibility,' we typically only issue full refunds within 30 days of the renewal date. However, I can see you have been a loyal customer for three years. Given your situation, I am authorized to make a one-time exception to this policy.
Oh, that would be wonderful. I really appreciate you working with me on this.

It is my pleasure, Todd. I have successfully processed a full refund of $49.99 to your card ending in 4492. You should see the credit reflect on your statement within 3-5 business days depending on your bank. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

resolution_summary: The agent verified the account and transaction, acknowledged the policy limit, but exercised discretionary authority to grant a one-time exception for a loyal customer, successfully issuing the refund.
